This question cost me a 27 LPA offer at KPMG 
The same question got me a 33 LPA offer at Deloitte.

In one interview, I was asked:
- How would you remove duplicate records from a huge PySpark DataFrame efficiently?

I froze. I didn’t know the answer. And yes, I got rejected. But instead of moving on, I went deeper into the questions and learned.

Two weeks later, I faced the same question in another interview. This time, I smiled and explained:

- Use dropDuplicates() if you want to remove duplicates based on all or specific columns.
- For very large datasets, repartition the DataFrame by key columns before deduplication to avoid expensive shuffles.
- Use window functions with row_number() if you need to keep the latest record per group.
- Cache intermediate results if reused, and tune spark.sql.shuffle.partitions for performance.
